summary: Extend the existing five-worktree guard to Codex native asynchronous worktree creation so its reservation survives until matching terminal evidence is verified.

gaps_found.gap: Codex native create_worktree and get_worktree_creation_status currently bypass the installed PreToolUse matcher and parser.
gaps_found.recommendation: Add exact native tool matchers and bind repository admission to tool invocation and async operation identity.

refined_plan.objective: Enforce the existing five-total-worktree and clean/landed admission rules for native asynchronous Codex worktree creation.
refined_plan.scope: Extend the canonical guard in the existing hooks checkout and PR #63 branch. Match native create and status tools, canonicalize sourceRoot, preserve an invocation reservation through asynchronous completion, and update exact tests and documentation.
non_goals: Do not change the cap, create or remove worktrees, merge branches, or touch live trading systems.
Do not claim coverage for external Git clients, arbitrary subprocesses, or host tools without callbacks.
Do not expire reservations by TTL or release them on missing or ambiguous evidence.

system_boundaries.integration_point: Codex PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks with tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id and tool_response.
Canonical Git common directory and git worktree list --porcelain.

steps.action: Read the native hook payload and validate exact tool name, tool_use_id, sourceRoot, repository identity, current worktree inventory, owner-intent token, and admission rules.
steps.deliverable: Fail-closed native create preflight with canonical repository binding.

steps.action: Persist the admitted invocation reservation; bind returned operationId and release only on exact matching completed/failed status. Verify a completed worktree appears in Git inventory before release.
steps.deliverable: Race-safe asynchronous reservation lifecycle and guarded recovery.

steps.action: Add callback fixtures, concurrency and mismatch tests, installer registration tests, and documented coverage/recovery limits.
steps.deliverable: Focused regression suite and operator documentation.

steps.action: Obtain independent source review, then run focused test and installer validation; update PR #63 and issue coordination with exact evidence.
steps.deliverable: Reviewed, verified patch ready for normal merge gates.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Native Codex create_worktree is matched in PreToolUse and runs the same five-tree, clean/landed, owner-intent and fail-closed repository admission checks as other covered creation paths.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Fixture callback tests at cap boundary, dirty/unlanded and malformed repository inputs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every admitted asynchronous create is bound to canonical repository identity and exact tool_use_id; returned operationId is persisted and the reservation stays held across PostToolUse when the tool returns pending.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Lifecycle tests for immediate terminal result, pending operationId, mismatched invocation and missing response.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Only a matching completed/failed status releases a reservation; completed status also requires the created worktree to be visible in Git inventory. Manual recovery requires exact sourceRoot, create tool_use_id, operationId and saved terminal response, including when the operation index is absent.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Status callback tests for success, failure, mismatch, unknown, nonterminal, and absent inventory evidence.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Installer tests register exact create/status hooks while preserving unrelated matcher groups and trust settings.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Temporary Codex hooks configuration integration test.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Documentation explains native asynchronous coverage, fail-closed conditions, guarded manual recovery and unsupported paths.

unit: Fixture tests for callback parsing, canonical repository identity, admission, reservation persistence, ID binding, terminal release and audit contents.
integration: Install into a temporary Codex hooks.json fixture and confirm create/status registration preserves unrelated hook entries and trust settings.
e2e: Do not create a real worktree; exercise documented callback fixtures and temporary Git repositories.
negative: Reject malformed/ambiguous sourceRoot, cap reached, dirty/unlanded inventory, missing token, duplicate/mismatched IDs, unknown/nonterminal status, and missing successful inventory readback.
regression: Run existing cap scratch-repository tests and installer tests; confirm Claude, shell and Codex Agent paths retain behavior.

risks: Untrusted callback fields could release another repository or operation reservation.
An incomplete callback could release the lock before the async worktree exists.
Audit data could expose prompts or credentials if payloads are logged wholesale.
controls: Bind each reservation to canonical Git common dir, exact tool_use_id and returned operationId.
Keep uncertain reservations fail-closed; release only on exact terminal status and verify inventory for completed operations.
Store only hashed repository/operation identifiers and status metadata; never log prompts or secrets.
security_review.secrets_handling: Do not read, persist or log secrets; callback logs contain only allowlisted metadata.
security_review.auth_requirements: Use the existing short-lived owner-intent token; do not claim native tool payloads prove human identity.
security_review.least_privilege: Hook reads repository metadata and writes only its own lock and audit state.

requirements: Local development workflow guard; no regulated data processing.
compliance_review.audit_trail: Reservation lifecycle records timestamp, hashed repository and operation IDs, terminal status, and recovery reason.

edge_cases.case: Four registered worktrees and a native create request
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Proceed only if all other admission checks pass and lock is acquired.

edge_cases.case: Five or more worktrees, dirty/unlanded checkout, or unavailable remote
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Refuse before native creation and state the concrete reason.

edge_cases.case: sourceRoot omitted or malformed and cwd cannot identify one Git repository
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Fail closed without consuming an unrelated repository token.

edge_cases.case: Native create returns operationId and PostToolUse fires before operation completion
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Keep the matching reservation until status becomes terminal.

edge_cases.case: Status callback is mismatched, unknown, or nonterminal
Completed status reports success but Git inventory lacks the worktree
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Keep reservation and report the inconsistency.

failure_modes.failure: Cannot resolve sourceRoot/cwd to one canonical repository.
failure_modes.recovery: Call with an absolute valid sourceRoot for the intended checkout.

failure_modes.failure: Cap or clean/landed admission check fails.
failure_modes.degradation: Native creation is denied with the blocking checkout path.
failure_modes.recovery: Resolve the existing worktree state through the repository release process, then retry.

failure_modes.failure: Operation ID or matching terminal status is missing.
failure_modes.degradation: Reservation remains held and later creates are denied for that repository.
failure_modes.recovery: Supply exact saved terminal status evidence through guarded recovery; do not clear by age.

failure_modes.failure: Completed status cannot be confirmed in Git inventory.
failure_modes.recovery: Reconcile the app operation with git worktree list and use exact operation-bound recovery.

logs: Record reservation created/bound/released and recovery events using hashed repository and operation IDs.
error_messages: Worktree creation denied: repository identity is ambiguous.
Worktree creation denied: five-worktree or clean/landed admission check failed.
Worktree reservation retained: matching terminal operation evidence is unavailable.

steps: Run code review before tests per repository contract.
Run focused hook and installer checks on the exact branch head.
Merge only through the repository-required exact-head gates.
Install from canonical source with the official installer, then read back hook registration and exercise a non-creating callback fixture.
rollback: Restore the previous canonical hook source through a reviewed revert.
Run the canonical installer to restore prior registrations and confirm readback.
deployment.backward_compatibility: Existing tool matchers and state records remain supported; native operation records are versioned and fail closed when unknown.

definition_of_done: Exact create and status hooks are installed by the canonical installer and preserve existing registrations.
Regression tests prove admission and reservation lifecycle including async and failure paths.
README documents supported boundaries and recovery.
Independent review, audit, CI and exact-head merge gates pass.

updates_needed: Update worktree-cap README coverage and async reservation/recovery behavior.
Update the canonical issue acceptance record with the newly covered native path.
documentation.changelog_entry: Add guarded coverage for Codex native asynchronous worktree creation.
documentation.ticket_notes: Keep the repository limit at five total registered worktrees.

proposed_ci_checks: Add drift test for exact native create/status hook registration.
Add callback tests proving mismatch and nonterminal status cannot release reservations.
agents_md_additions: Native async worktree reservations stay held until exact matching terminal evidence and Git inventory readback are verified.
